newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton market closed for Hindu festival.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton market closed for Hindu festival.

text.p: The Bombay cotton market was closed on Wednesday for a Hindu festival.
On Tuesday cotton prices fell on sluggish buying by mills and improved arrivals.
They said arrivals picked up considerably after a strike by truck operators was called off last week.
In spot, Bengal-deshi fell 15/20 rupees to 880/925 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned lost 45 rupees to 1,500/1,640 rupees per maund.

Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) shed 600 rupees to 12,900/13,100 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 (the average variety) lost 200/500 rupees to 15,500/17,000 rupees per candy and to 18,000/19,300 rupees per candy for the superior variety.
